But a new paper from an international group of scientists working with the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) Collaboration, recently published in The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series, takes a stab at closing that gap by identifying 450 cosmic sources in the 20–200 MeV range, providing the clearest view of low-energy gamma rays ever.

items.title: What makes rock deep beneath continents break away and sink?

But deep beneath some mountain belts and volcanic arcs, the opposite can happen: dense rock at the base of the crust can become unstable, break away and sink hundreds of kilometers into the mantle, dragging part of the rigid outer shell of the Earth (the lithosphere) with it. Seismic images suggest that this process, known as lithospheric dripping, has occurred beneath the central Andes and California's Sierra Nevada.

items.title: Homologs of the Major Vault Protein defend bacteria against ribotoxins
items.blurb: Bacteria use sophisticated mechanisms to defend themselves against antibiotics and bacteriophages, yet how they combat toxins deployed during interbacterial competition remains poorly understood. Bacteria use type VI secretion, bacteriocins, and contact dependent inhibition systems to deliver antibacterial toxins that inhibit growth by antagonizing essential processes. Here, we discover that Pseudomonas aeruginosa uses homologs of the eukaryotic major vault protein and a tRNA-like noncoding RNA to defend against RNA-damaging ribotoxins. Using an engineered pyocin delivery system, we showed that P. aeruginosa sensed ribotoxin damage and activated transcription of an RNA repair operon, which included band7, a homolog of the major vault protein. Genetic analyses demonstrated that band7-expressing bacteria were significantly more protected against growth inhibition by a ribotoxin that cleaved the anticodon loop of specific tRNA. Band7 was necessary but not sufficient, and defense also required a non-coding band7 RNA (bRNA). bRNA was cleaved by the ribotoxin, suggesting a mechanism for specificity and defense. Bioinformatic analyses revealed that band7 and candidate bRNA are widely distributed within RNA repair systems across diverse bacteria. Our data suggest that bacteria use structures related to the eukaryotic vault complex to respond to RNA damage thereby providing a hypothesis for the function of the enigmatic human vault.

items.title: Mapping Senescence Landscapes in Metabolic Liver Disease Progression
items.blurb: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects more than 30% of the population, often progressing from reversible steatosis to irreversible fibrosis and cirrhosis. Although cellular senescence is implicated in driving MASLD, the evidence in human tissue and the mechanism are lacking. Here, we apply spatial transcriptomics and scRNAseq to human liver samples spanning healthy to fibrotic disease to address these knowledge gaps. Using a combination of cell stress, cell cycle arrest, extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, and inflammatory genes, senescent microenvironments termed "SenSpots" were identified by Visium transcriptomics that predominantly localized to portal tracts and fibrotic septa across all specimens. Functional profiling revealed a fundamental phenotypic divergence: SenSpots in healthy liver displayed a physiological wound-healing and tissue-development program, whereas SenSpots in fibrotic tissue expressed genes related to inflammation, stress, and ECM-disassembly. Spatial deconvolution and network expansion analyses demonstrated that SenSpots act as epicenters for TGF-{beta}, NOTCH, complement, and ECM-reorganization signaling, which spreads into the surrounding tissue microenvironment as disease advances. Furthermore, scRNAseq data validated the Visium results and identified a previously unappreciated population of senescent Schwann cells in the diseased liver niche. These findings map the spatial origination and paracrine propagation of pathological senescence and identify senotypes associated with liver fibrosis.

items.title: Caenorhabditis elegans HLH-30/TFEB has age-dependent effects on the transcriptome and is required for normal progeny number and larval survival under basal growth conditions
items.blurb: Background: The transcription factor TFEB/HLH-30 is a well-established regulator of autophagy and lysosomal biogenesis during starvation and stress, and it plays important roles in development and homeostasis. Our previous work demonstrated that Caenorhabditis elegans HLH-30 also functions under basal physiological conditions in mature neurons, where it promotes the expansion of endo-lysosomal degradative capacity during early adulthood. These findings raised the question of whether HLH-30 promotes lysosomal gene expression more broadly during early adulthood, and, more generally, whether its basal transcriptional functions depend on animal age. To address these questions, we analyzed the impact of hlh-30 loss on the transcriptome at two larval stages, L1 and L4, and two adult ages, Day 3 and Day 6, in hermaphrodites grown under basal conditions. Results: We identified modest effects of hlh-30 loss on the transcriptome that varied by stage/age. Enrichment analyses of genes downregulated in hlh-30 mutants identified functions related to defense response at L1 and in adulthood, and to cuticle development in adulthood. On the other hand, a role for hlh-30 in the basal expression of autophagy genes was exclusively detected in L1 larvae. A subset of genes encoding cathepsins showed decreased expression in the adult hlh-30 mutant; however, our results indicate that HLH-30 is not broadly required for basal expression of most lysosome biogenesis genes in adulthood. We also detected a trend toward reduced expression of genes involved in germline function at the L4 stage, when spermatogenesis occurs, and found that loss of hlh-30 resulted in reduced sperm and progeny numbers. In addition, we found that hlh-30 is required for full progeny survival through larval development. Finally, we identified a gene with increased expression at all four stages in the hlh-30 mutant, the germline transcription factor-encoding ztf-28. Knockdown of ztf-28 partially suppressed the reductions in progeny number and survival, suggesting that its increased expression contributes to these phenotypes. Conclusions: This study reveals roles for HLH-30 in transcriptome regulation under basal growth conditions that vary in both magnitude and content by animal age. Further, it demonstrates a previously unappreciated requirement for HLH-30 in promoting progeny number and survival, broadening our understanding of the physiological roles of this conserved transcription factor.

items.title: Sexual competition can select for male-only semelparity
items.blurb: Semelparity, - reproducing once in a lifetime - is an extreme solution to the trade-off between reproduction and future survival and is exceedingly rare in terrestrial vertebrates. Males of the Australian genera Antechinus, Phascogale and Dasykaluta are obligately semelparous while females are iteroparous, suggesting that the sexes face such different selective pressures that they have evolved different solutions to the same trade-off. Using invasion analyses of a novel two-sex population model with continuous reproductive investment, we show that the geometry of the reproduction-survival trade-off determines whether semelparity is evolutionarily accessible, but not necessarily whether it evolves. Age-structured survival and fecundity may maintain iteroparity under trade-off shapes for which classical theory predicts semelparity. Early onset of post-reproductive mortality can flip otherwise iteroparous trade-offs to semelparity, but only when survival declines quickly after sexual maturity. In contrast, when sexual competition gives high-investing males sufficiently disproportionate paternity, male-only semelparity can evolve under any trade-off geometry we examined, while females remain iteroparous. That male-only semelparity is rare while male competition is common suggests that lethal male investment evolves only under a particular combination of demographic, environmental and mating-system conditions.

items.title: Precision Fermentation Gets a New Player: Genome Assembly and Genetic Transformation of a Novel Strain, Pichia hangzhouana, for Precision Fermentation of Food Ingredients
items.blurb: Precision fermentation leverages the metabolic pathways of microorganisms to produce valuable proteins and enzymes. Pichia hangzhouana, synonymous with Zygoascus hellenicus, is a non-conventional yeast with potential for food biotechnological applications. This study characterizes the CSIRO strain P. hangzhouana FRR5246, isolated from a tea beverage, to evaluate its suitability as a precision fermentation host for a variety of industrial, agricultural and food production applications. P. hangzhouana demonstrated robust growth across a range of carbon sources, with the highest optical density observed in media containing sucrose or sorbitol as sole carbon source. The yeast showed susceptibility to geneticin, hygromycin B, nourseothricin sulfate, and zeocin sulfate antibiotic agents. Successful genetic transformation was achieved, with the expression of a recombinant orange fluorescent protein (OFP) under the control of the native glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAP1) promoter. The secretome exhibited strong antimicrobial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, indicating the presence of potent antimicrobial compounds. In addition, whole genome sequencing of P. hangzhouana FRR5246 provided genetic tools for recombinant expression of heterologous genes, insight into the genes, genetic architecture and regulatory mechanisms underlying phenotypic qualities, as well as confirming phylogenetic classification of this strain as clustering with the Dipodascomycetes, most closely related to species Zygoascus hellenicus. P. hangzhouana FRR5246 is a promising candidate for precision fermentation of food ingredients, capable of utilizing diverse carbon sources and producing recombinant proteins. In addition, production of antimicrobial compounds further enhances the potential for biotechnological exploitation. Future work will focus on optimizing growth conditions and exploring native inducible promoters for controlled gene expression.

items.title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics and Environmental Drivers of Maize Microbiome Structure across Diverse Agroecosystems in Georgia, USA
items.blurb: The understanding of how microbial communities differ across soils, environments, plant tissues, and developmental stages is key to the improvement of crop productivity and resilience. Here, we conducted a statewide survey of maize (Zea mays L.) microbiomes across 35 fields at 16 locations in Georgia, USA, sampling soil, rhizosphere, root interior, and stalk interior at two developmental stages (600 and 1400 growing degree days, GDD). More than 38000 ASVs were produced after amplicon sequencing of 16S rRNA genes. The phyla shown to be dominant are Proteobacteria, Actinobacteriota, Chloroflexi, Planctomycetota, and Acidobacteriota. Based on alpha and beta diversity analyses, the below-ground compartments (soil and rhizosphere) revealed higher diversity and stronger spatial structuring when compared to the above-ground sample types, whereas root and stalk interior microbiomes revealed marked shifts across growth stages. Amino acid metabolism, secondary metabolite biosynthesis, and energy-related pathways predictions (via PICRUSt2) show stage-dependent enrichment. Network analyses show persistent keystone taxa (Proteobacteria and Actinobacteriota) mediating microbial stability, coupled with an increase in modularity and connectivity as we move from early to late growth stages. Some environmental variables, such as temperature, humidity, soil potassium, and soil sodium, showed significant correlation with microbial diversity indicative of a compartment-specific environmental sensitivity. Collectively, our results show that in maize, microbial community composition, interaction, and potential functionality are both impacted by developmental stages and environmental heterogeneity. This study provides a fundamental framework for understanding the microbiome dynamics in field-grown maize across various agroecological conditions. It equally provides ecological insights relevant to microbiome-informed crop management.

items.title: Resident liver macrophages buffer dietary and circulating cholesterol to maintain hepatocyte homeostasis
items.blurb: Cholesterol metabolism is viewed largely through the lens of hepatocytes, leaving the roles of other liver cells unclear. Using high-resolution live imaging and cholesterol tracing in intact zebrafish, complemented by genetic and clodronate-mediated macrophage depletion and single-cell analysis, we identify liver-resident macrophages (LMs) as cellular buffers of circulating and dietary cholesterol. LMs directly take up cholesterol, and their depletion redirects cholesterol to hepatocytes, which suppress cholesterol synthesis, increase bile-acid synthesis and efflux, and activate metabolic-stress and immune programs, including hepatokine lect2 induction. These responses are heightened by elevated dietary cholesterol and occur without overt inflammation or altered liver architecture. LMs partition cholesterol through abca1b-dependent export and cetp-mediated lipoprotein remodeling. Loss of abca1b causes cholesterol sequestration in LMs and reduced cholesterol-processing demand on hepatocytes, while LM depletion eliminates macrophage-derived cetp and reduces hepatocyte cetp. Together, these findings reveal the innate immune system as integral to normal metabolic physiology, with LMs buffering cholesterol to maintain hepatocyte homeostasis.

items.title: Neural competition predicts speech production advantages in congenital amusia
items.blurb: Mental health research has traditionally been deficit-focused, and cognitive advantages in mental conditions have almost always been documented retrospectively. Here we propose and test an a priori pathway for predicting such advantages from a condition's impaired neural basis, neural competition and brain-mind associations. Using congenital amusia (CA), a neurodevelopmental disorder with a well-defined deficit in right frontotemporal circuit (FTC), as a model, we predicted that interhemispheric competition would release the left homologue from inhibition, conferring advantages in speech production. Two independent studies, multimodal neuroimaging and behavioral testing, confirmed this prediction: MRI revealed right FTC impairment alongside competitive-like benefits of the left FTC in CA; and CA showed speech production advantages with intact episodic memory and constrained music learning. These findings provide the first empirical demonstration that cognitive advantages can be predicted in advance and then verified, offering a principled, mechanism-based alternative to the deficit-focused paradigm.

items.title: Gene regulatory networks and the organization of cell differentiation in multicellular organisms
items.blurb: Across their development, clonal multicellular organisms generate new cell types from less differentiated cell types. Differentiation pathways arrange into a hierarchical, tree-like organization: regressions from specialized to undifferentiated cell types rarely occur and undifferentiated cell types often have the potential to produce, when subject to distinct stimuli, two or more differently specialized cell types. How cell type transitions acquire such a peculiar disposition requires an explanation that must reside in the properties of gene regulatory networks (GRNs); after all, GRNs orchestrate the changes in gene activity that define cell types. We studied vast numbers of small dynamic model networks to search for elementary GRNs that could yield the simplest hierarchical, developmental-like, differentiation patterns. We found that only a small minority of GRNs are compatible with hierarchical cell type transitions. Importantly, GRNs that yielded developmental-like differentiation patterns shared common traits: One is the presence of tangles of cycles of positive interactions. Genes in such a tangle produce an all-or-none one-way response to a signal. Another such trait is mutual inhibition between genes associated to different specialized cell types, enforcing their mutually exclusive activation. Moreover, these regulatory patterns are more abundant in published experimentally sustained developmental GRNs than as expected by chance. In addition, we show that it is easy to maintain hierarchical cellular differentiation throughout evolution, even when undergoing changes in gene regulatory interactions and developmental mechanisms. Our work supports the prevalence of design principles that organize hierarchically differentiation pathways in clonal multicellular organisms.

items.title: Hearts in sync on a roller coaster: heart-rate responses, synchrony and psychological change in 439 amusement-park riders
items.blurb: Background Shared intense experiences are thought to bring people closer, and synchronized physiology is a proposed reason. We examined heart rate and synchrony across ride phases, riders' response profiles, and whether these relate to changes in happiness, stress and closeness. Methods In this exploratory field study we recorded heart rate in 439 riders (418 with usable data) on 19 trains of the Balder roller coaster, Gothenburg, Sweden, and measured happiness, stress and closeness (0-10) just before and after the ride. Real pairs were compared with surrogate pairs from different trains, aligned on ride start, to separate coupling between riders from the ride's own effect. Profiles came from k-means clustering; analyses used linear mixed models. Results Heart rate rose by 15.2 beats per minute (95% CI 14.2 to 16.3) during the two-minute ride and was back at baseline within nine minutes. Heart-rate curves did not form clearly distinct types (two profiles, silhouette 0.29): riders calm in the queue rose more and stayed elevated, while riders already aroused rose less. Pairs in which both riders came with companions gained more synchrony during the ride than the surrogate benchmark (Fisher z 0.096, 95% CI 0.050 to 0.142); for pairs including a solo rider the boost was smaller and uncertain. This coupling peaked just after the ride and was gone five minutes later. Riders reported being happier (+1.3 points, Cohen's d = 0.87) and closer to the other riders on the train (+2.2 points, d = 0.70). Neither phase-specific heart-rate responses, response profile nor synchrony was associated with these changes. Conclusions A short shared thrill coupled riders' heart rates beyond what the ride alone explains, and riders felt happier and closer to others on the train afterwards, but the two ran in parallel. Without a non-riding comparison, the psychological changes cannot be attributed to the ride itself.

items.title: GPU handling of OPC water in GROMACS: validation by protein folding and a 1.6-fold speed-up
items.blurb: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation is one of the core computational methods of the life sciences, used to study protein folding, receptor activation and drug binding in atomic detail. The timescales it can reach depend on speed, and running each step entirely on a graphics processing unit (GPU) is now essential for fast simulation. Optimal Point Charge (OPC) water, recommended for the ff19SB protein force field, carries its negative charge on a virtual site, and in GROMACS 2026.3 virtual sites prevent the coordinate update from running on the GPU. The GROMACS developers have recently added GPU handling of virtual sites to the development version as an experimental feature. Whether simulations run in this way agree with the established CPU calculation has to be measured, and no such test has been reported over microseconds or in a membrane-protein system of production size. We compared a modified build that handles OPC sites within the GPU update (Optimized) with the official release (Reference). The two builds placed the charge site with the same error (2.3 x 10^-7 nm) and gave relative force differences below 10^-6. In five matched pairs of 5-microsecond simulations, the Trp-cage miniprotein folded with both builds (three of five Reference and five of five Optimized runs; P = 0.44), and the folded ensembles matched. Both builds reproduced the density, diffusion coefficient, dielectric constant and second hydration shell that distinguish OPC from TIP3P water. In a 166,826-atom membrane system of the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor, residue hydration agreed between the builds (r = 0.99), and Optimized ran 1.57-1.66 times as fast as tuned Reference on two GPUs, with 87-97% of the time saved coming from moving the coordinate update to the GPU. In these tests, GPU handling of OPC sites gave a substantial speed gain with no sign of altered physical behaviour.

items.title: Sequence-Derived Geometric Priors Enable Controllable Generation of Intrinsically Disordered Protein Ensembles
items.blurb: Predicting heterogeneous conformational ensembles from sequence remains a central challenge for intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs). Sequence-to-ensemble models often entangle geometric inference with coordinate generation, obscuring error sources and limiting control over ensemble properties. Here we introduce MANTA, a C-level framework that separates these stages. An encoder derives geometric priors from protein language-model representations, and a graph-Laplacian decoder converts these priors into conformational ensembles. On a homology-held-out test set, replacing predicted priors with reference-derived priors under the same decoder reduces the median absolute relative radius-of-gyration error from 8.78% to 1.89%, identifying geometric-prior estimation as the dominant bottleneck in MANTA. Across an external benchmark of 27 IDPs, MANTA generates broad, locally valid ensembles. Decoder controls modulate mean compactness and conformational breadth along partially separable axes, while compactness modulation alters motif exposure in tau and amyloid-{beta}. Meanwhile, -synuclein variants shift local exposure populations at nearly unchanged global size. MANTA provides a diagnostic and controllable framework for ensemble generation that captures both global dimensions and local conformational organization.

items.title: SIREN: Predicting RNA-Small Molecule Interaction using Language Models without Requiring Structure
items.blurb: RNA-targeted drug discovery is constrained by the scarcity of resolved RNA tertiary structures and the conformational flexibility of RNA, which limit the applicability of structure-based virtual screening. Here, SIREN (Small molecule Interaction with RNA via sEquence-based predictioN) is presented, a sequence-based framework that ranks small molecules for a given RNA target directly from its primary sequence without requiring tertiary structure. SIREN integrates a pretrained RNA language model with molecular language model embeddings and physicochemical descriptors through an interaction network that outputs a target-specific compound-ranking score. On four held-out ROBIN riboswitch targets, SIREN outperforms the structure-based methods RNAmigos2, RNAmigos++, and rDock in both enrichment and overall discrimination, and a cross-target derangement analysis confirms that its rankings depend on RNA identity rather than general ligand propensity alone. On an independent HIV-1 TAR benchmark, SIREN achieves strong discrimination without an experimentally derived RNA conformational ensemble. Prospective screening against IRES-derived RNA hairpins from cMyc and XIAP mRNAs further identifies multiple experimentally validated, micromolar-affinity binders from a diverse chemical library. These results demonstrate that SIREN generalizes to unseen RNA targets, transfers across independent benchmarks, and provides a scalable, structure-free framework for RNA-targeted compound prioritization that complements existing structure-based screening approaches.

items.title: Period-Specific Remodeling of Luminal Lineages and the Mammary Microenvironment in Dairy Goats
items.blurb: Milk production requires coordinated remodeling of mammary epithelial lineages and their stromal and immune niches, but this process is incompletely resolved in dairy goats. We aim to define period specific cell states and epithelial niche interactions across the dry to lactation transition. We profile mammary tissue from three peak-lactation and three dry-period Saanen goats using 10x Genomics single-cell RNA sequencing and map one peak-lactation goat with Stereo-seq. Among 44,120 cells, we identify15 populations. Peak lactation is characterized by expansion of luminal alveolar cells and increased {beta}-casein and -lactalbumin expression, whereas luminal progenitors, hormone-sensing cells, fibroblasts, and B cells are enriched in the dry period. Trajectory inference place luminal progenitors near branches toward alveolar and hormone-sensing states, with sustained ELF5-associated activity along the alveolar branch. Myoepithelial, macrophage, natural killer T, and T cell states are also remodeled. SPP1 and MIF signaling networks become more connected and change their cellular targets. These data establish a period resolved atlas of dairy goat mammary remodeling and identify coordinated epithelial, stromal, immune, and communication programs associated with active lactation.

items.title: RR3DD 2.0: an expanded database for RNA three-dimensional structure classification
items.blurb: RNA performs diverse biological functions by folding into specific 3D structures, which are often more conserved than their sequences. Systematic classification of RNA 3D structures is fundamental to understanding structure-function relationships. We previously established RR3DD, the first classification database based on global 3D structural similarity. However, its version 1.0 contained data only up to July 2021 and can no longer reflect the rapidly growing RNA structure space since then. Here, we present RR3DD 2.0. Starting from the 7,466 PDB-format chains in 1.0, we incorporated 8,298 newly released or updated chains, expanding the dataset to 15,764 chains. Pairwise structural similarity (RMscore) was calculated using RMalign, and all chains were re-clustered to yield 1,042 clusters. Compared with 1.0, 2.0 not only increases sampling density but also identifies 342 new clusters. Notably, Cluster-891 and Cluster-899 correspond to the ROOL RNA and GOLLD RNA families, marking the first inclusion of these large structured bacterial ncRNAs into a global classification framework. Mapping the clusters to Rfam annotated 6,388 chains (40.5%) across 154 families. A single cluster can correspond to one or several Rfam families, indicating that global structure classification and sequence family classification are complementary. RR3DD 2.0 provides an updated web interface.

items.title: Replicate libraries set the noise floor for cell-state claims in cross-sectional single-cell data: an empirical audit in drug-tolerant EGFR-mutant PC9 cells
items.blurb: Claims that drug-tolerant cancer cells occupy stable states rest on single-cell snapshots with one sequencing library per condition, where a difference between conditions cannot be separated from a difference between libraries. No standard says how far a contrast must exceed replicate-library variation. We contribute a replicate-referenced framework: a distance ratio expressing a contrast as a multiple of the distance between replicate libraries of one condition, and a library-level permutation test giving exact p values by relabelling whole libraries. In simulations, single-library tests and a split-half reference rejected a true null in 99 to 100% of runs, and Harmony followed by a cell-level test did so in 12 to 32% with structured library effects. With four libraries per arm, the library-level test held false positives at 3 to 5% in every setting. In public osimertinib-treated PC9 data with two libraries per condition (GSE150949), halves of one library were indistinguishable, replicate libraries separated at 59 to 93% accuracy, and contrasts between times in drug and sort gates exceeded replicate distance 4.5- to 51-fold. In Drop-seq erlotinib data with one library per condition (GSE149383), two libraries of the same condition separated more readily (93.3%) than withdrawn and re-treated cells (88.5%). Cross-sectional contrasts should be reported as multiples of replicate-library distance and, with four or more libraries per arm, tested by library-level permutation. Cells moved away from the untreated profile and stayed away, but the data do not support attractor-style inference, nor do they show that tolerant states are not bistable.

items.title: Mass Transfer Formulations Shape Oxygen Transport and Tissue Oxygenation in Microvascular Networks
items.blurb: Continuous oxygen delivery is essential for cerebral tissue function, yet its local supply characteristics remain incompletely understood. Quantifying oxygen transport in microvascular networks (MVNs) requires a physiologically consistent description of oxygen exchange between vascular compartments via mass transfer coefficients (MTCs). We investigate how different MTC formulations influence oxygen availability and hypoxic burden in realistic MVNs, and whether they produce relevant local differences in tissue oxygenation. A multicompartment oxygen transport model describing exchange between red blood cells (RBCs), plasma, and tissue in realistic MVNs was developed and evaluated against in vivo measurements. Three RBC-plasma MTC formulations were compared: constant, hematocrit-dependent, and hematocrit- and saturation-dependent. Additionally, a double-flux formulation incorporating a direct RBC-to-tissue flux was compared with standard single-flux formulations. Global tissue oxygen distributions were comparable across RBC-plasma MTC formulations, but hematocrit- and saturation-dependent MTC formulations predicted larger hypoxic tissue fractions. The largest differences occurred under low hematocrit, with local plasma oxygen partial pressure PO2 differing by {approx}6 mmHg along representative vascular paths. Introducing the direct RBC-tissue exchange reduced tissue PO2 at low hematocrit and enhanced it at high hematocrit, with the largest differences observed in small vessels. Sensitivity analysis revealed that RBC oxygen diffusivity can alter the double-flux effect magnitude. MTC assumptions substantially influence predicted oxygen availability and hypoxic burden, particularly under low-hematocrit conditions and in small vessels, underlining the need for their accurate definition. The proposed model provides a basis for evaluating these effects, improving the interpretation of oxygen transport predictions in realistic MVNs.

items.title: A midnight snack for spirulina: a dual-substrate kinetic model for second cheese whey supplementation of Arthrospira platensis
items.blurb: Arthrospira platensis (Spirulina) is a widely used strategic cyanobacterium whose cultivation cost remains a primary barrier to large-scale production. Mixotrophic growth on dairy by-products offers a simultaneous route to increase biomass concentration and valorize industrial waste streams. Here, we investigate the effect of Parmigiano Reggiano second cheese whey supplementation on A. platensis batch cultivation under continuous and alternating photoperiods. Whey supplementation increased final biomass in a dose-dependent manner under both continuous and alternating light. At the higher supplementation level, cultures under alternating light reached the same final biomass as under continuous illumination within the cultivation window. To interpret the interaction between whey availability, photoperiod, and biomass accumulation, we developed a kinetic model in which inorganic substrate assimilation is light-dependent, while whey-associated growth can contribute during both light and dark phases through a phenomenological dark-phase coefficient. Model and experimental results are consistent with the assumption that photoperiod mainly modulates the rate of biomass accumulation rather than the attainable biomass, under sufficient substrate availability. These results support a nutrient-stoichiometric interpretation of the biomass ceiling and suggest that second cheese whey supplementation can reduce dependence on continuous artificial lighting, providing a promising route for more resource-efficient Arthrospira cultivation.

items.title: Modeling Aerobic-Anaerobic Microbial Electrolysis Cells for Multi-step Methane Conversion
items.blurb: The bioconversion of methane by anaerobic methanotrophs has a higher carbon and energy efficiency compared to aerobic processes, suggesting significant potential for producing value-added chemicals and reducing green-house-gas emissions. However, their practical use still faces many challenges regarding their culturing, genetic manipulation, and integration into multi-species consortia. Here we mathematically model a microbial electrolysis cell (MEC) to study the division of labor inside an anode-attached vertically stratified biofilm, where genetically modified Methanosarcina acetivorans and Escherichia coli perform the anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM) to acetate followed by the aerobic conversion to 2,3-butanediol, respectively. We find that such a design is theoretically feasible, and we identify minimum biological improvements and operational conditions so that the aerobic layer effectively acts as oxygen-consuming living membrane protecting the anaerobic layer. Considering current biotechnological parameters points to a significant yet feasible need for further microbial engineering to increase the AOM rate. A comparison to a more traditional two-stage reactor at equivalent biomass reveals advantages and drawbacks of both designs, e.g., tradeoffs between peak product yield, reactor volume, and operational complexity. These results inform AOM driven microbial upgrading via aerobic-anaerobic stratified biofilms as well as value-added production via cooperative consortia in general.

items.title: Molecular Conformer Sampling Beyond Generations
items.blurb: Sampling the low-energy conformational states available to a molecule is a fundamental problem in computational chemistry and drug discovery, since molecular properties and downstream design decisions depend on the relevant three-dimensional geometries rather than on a single structure. Recent diffusion and flow-based generative models can efficiently sample conformer candidates from molecular graphs, but under a fixed output budget their samples do not cover the full set of relevant conformational states of a molecule, while practical benchmarks and downstream applications require a small ensemble that is both diverse and physically plausible. We present a post-generation selection framework that turns candidate pools from frozen, pre-trained generators into compact conformer ensembles without any retraining or fine-tuning of the underlying generator. The framework offers two selectors that share the same candidate pool and the same learned reference-likelihood classifier: CovSelect, a coverage-maximizing selector that greedily reaches as many distinct reference states as the pool allows, and RefSelect, a tunable selector that trades some of that coverage for higher precision and, at its balanced setting, matches or exceeds strong generative baselines on both measures at once. On the full GEOM-DRUGS test set, CovSelect reaches 91.33% mean recall (98.36% median), outperforming every raw generator we compare against, and RefSelect at its balanced setting exceeds the strongest raw baseline, DMT-L, on both recall and precision. Finally, across several out of distribution benchmarks (QMugs, pepconf, and Platinum), CovSelect substantially outperforms all raw generative baselines in recall and precision.

items.title: A recombinant expression system for the Variant Surface Glycoproteins enables structural elucidation of challenging classes of trypanosome proteins
items.blurb: The African Trypanosome (Trypanosoma brucei) persists in the mammalian host by periodically altering its surface coat with antigenically distinct versions of the Variant Surface Glycoprotein (VSG). This process is called antigenic variation and produces repeated cycles of immune clearance and parasite VSG switching, leading to high morbidity and mortality in the absence of chemotherapeutic intervention. Elucidating how variant VSGs evade immune clearance is thus central to understanding trypanosomiasis. Progress in studying the large repertoire of thousands of VSG proteins has been hindered by the challenge of producing these coat proteins. Here we report the use of suspension HEK293 cells for this purpose, a system with robust yields that preserves many key elements of VSG structure and post-translational modifications, verified by expressing, purifying, and determining the crystal structures of the well-characterized proteins VSG2 and VSG3. We then applied this heterologous expression system to the production of several VSGs that had failed to express natively in T. brucei, including truncated VSG-Related Proteins (VRPs) from T. brucei and VSGs from T. vivax. This allowed for the determination of the structures of the T. brucei VRP VSG1619 as well as the VSG F9WSW0 from Trypanosoma vivax (T. vivax). The structure of VSG1619 shows similarities to the upper-lobe structures of B-class VSGs, but the monomers do not assemble into either the typical A-class dimer or B-class trimer in solution or in the crystals. The structure of T. vivax F9WSW0 is notable as a divergent member of the Class-A group that was developed from structures of T. brucei VSGs, with a canonical dimer but differences in fold, disulfide placement, and N-linked glycosylation. The described expression system provides additional insight into the family of VRPs and opens the door to general progress with the VSGs of more divergent trypanosome species through recombinant protein production.

items.title: Evaluating cell-free RNA extraction platforms for RNA liquid biopsy via nanopore sequencing
items.blurb: RNA liquid biopsies provide systemic insights into health and disease by profiling cell-free RNAs (cfRNAs) secreted into the circulation. While cfRNAs are thought to be short or fragmented, recent efforts using long-read nanopore sequencing have found that thousands of longer, full-length cfRNAs are highly abundant in plasma. However, cfRNA extraction methods have not been rigorously evaluated to assess reproducibility, cfRNA length, and transcriptome complexity. Here we show that extraction workflow is a major source of variation by comparing identical plasma samples across three different cfRNA extraction platforms. While these platforms recover comparable quantities of cfRNA, we perform nanopore sequencing to show that they differ in their cfRNA composition based on read-length distribution and biotype representation. Principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering of variable protein-coding and repeat-derived cfRNAs show that samples tend to cluster based on extraction platform. Robust detection of specific biotypes is contingent on extraction platform, as evidenced by significant enrichment of Alu element- and long noncoding RNA (lncRNA)-derived cfRNAs in some but not all methodologies. Our results reveal that cfRNA extraction platforms influence the composition and complexity of downstream libraries, highlighting the importance of selecting the right platform for profiling disease-relevant biomarkers in RNA liquid biopsy studies.

items.title: A genetic toolkit of visible mutants for Caenorhabditis briggsae
items.blurb: Caenorhabditis briggsae is a widely used model for comparative genetic studies involving C. elegans. Genetic analysis in C. briggsae depends on mutations with clear, easily recognizable phenotypes, yet most mutants reported so far have been mentioned only as names and linkage groups, without underlying experimental data. This study reports 183 C. briggsae mutants belonging to 11 phenotypic classes, which represent the most comprehensive collection to date. Almost all mutants were recovered in EMS screens of the reference strain AF16. Our analysis revealed that 121 mutations define 55 loci and 62 remain unassigned. A combination of complementation tests, linkage tests, two- and three-factor crosses, and polymorphism-based mappings helped place 51 loci and 15 further mutations to the six linkage groups. We report the supporting data, map distances, linkage groups, and corrections to several earlier assignments. Twenty-three loci correspond to molecularly identified orthologs of C. elegans genes, including six for which we report genetic, rescue, or sequence evidence here. The levamisole-resistant mutants fall into at least three complementation groups, two of which correspond to Cbr-unc-38 and Cbr-unc-29 (levamisole-sensitive nicotinic acetylcholine receptor a and non-a subunit, respectively). Transgene rescue experiments identify Cbr-dpy-1 (mucin-like), Cbr-sma-6 (TGFb type receptor kinase), and Cbr-unc-4 (homeodomain transcription factor), genes that have long been in use as genetic markers. In all cases, molecularly identified genes are located on the same chromosome as their C. elegans orthologs, although gene order within chromosomes differs. The strains, map, and underlying data provide a resource for genetic and comparative studies in Caenorhabditis nematodes.

items.title: Individual symbiont strains can compensate for complex microbiome loss in the bull-headed dung beetle, Onthophagus taurus
items.blurb: Many animals and plants have evolved to rely on microbiome mediated interactions with their environment. Across diverse insect groups, many are incapable of either breaking down complex carbohydrates or synthesizing essential nutrients despite consuming diets which should require one, or both, functions. Onthophagus beetles are one such host, with recent work suggesting their ability to digest their dung diet, typically rich in tough to digest polysaccharides and poor in nutrients, is likely bolstered by heritable symbionts. Despite there being over 2,000 species of Onthophagus, and over 5,000 species of "true" dung beetles (Scarabaeinae), little is known about how the microbiomes of these beetles modulate their interactions with their dung diet. The work presented here assesses the possible significance of four individual microbiome members, present during Onthophagus taurus development. Results show that three of the four isolates tested partially recovered normative developmental outcomes in O. taurus. Specifically, inoculation with a strain of either Acinetobacter, Brucella, or Pseudomonas increased pupal size relative to beetles deprived of the maternal inoculate. This mirrors the effects of individuals receiving the full natural inoculate, which contains hundreds of bacterial species. Further, using whole genome sequencing, we form a hypothesis of what nutrients these isolates provide to benefit O. taurus development. The findings presented here further highlight Onthophagus dung beetles as powerful systems to study the complex ways in which microbiome function can interact with diet to influence developmental and evolutionary outcomes.

items.title: Large-scale 3D stitching montage cryo-electron tomography reveals heterogeneity and connectivity of lamellipodial actin networks
items.blurb: Cellular processes range from local interactions among a few proteins to micrometer-scale assemblies whose coordinated components give rise to emergent properties. A prime example is the actin cytoskeleton in protrusive structures at the leading edge of migrating cells, termed lamellipodia. Significant progress has been made in understanding the functional contributions of distinct actin-filament populations and associated proteins within lamellipodia. Yet, a detailed quantitative appreciation of how actin filaments form a spatially connected and interdependent network has been impeded by limitations of existing methods. Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) can visualize such biological entities at molecular resolution in native cellular environments, but its limited field-of -view constrains quantitative analysis of extended assemblies. Hence, how lamellipodial actin architectures collectively support productive migration is not completely understood. Here, we present a 3D stitching montage cryo-ET workflow that advances both methodological and biological frontiers through its application to lamellipodia. We combine large-area montage-tilt series acquisition with independent tile reconstruction, denoising, and optical flow-based three-dimensional stitching to reconstruct large regions of the leading edge up to ~ 100 m2 at single-filament resolution. Bridging molecular resolution and cellular-scale context allows comprehensive filament tracing and quantification of actin filament networks, providing parameters for models of force generation in motile cells. Our data reveal that the network architecture in a seemingly uniform protrusive lamellipodium is markedly heterogeneous. By mapping Arp2/3 branch junction-based connectivity, using the molecular resolution of our data, we show how branch-junction distribution and network connectivity vary as a function of filament density and distance from the leading edge. We also identify the complex coexistence of short, branched and long, unbranched filament assemblies. We provide montage 3D volumes and filament vectorizations through an interactive, open web-based resource for browsing and interrogating the data. Our work thus provides a quantitative reference for lamellipodial actin architecture and a scalable approach for large-scale cryo-ET.

items.title: Inactive X chromosome DNA methylation erosion with age in human dermal fibroblasts
items.blurb: X chromosome inactivation is an epigenetic process that establishes dosage compensation between the sexes through the monoallelic silencing of one X chromosome in karyotypically normal females. The allele that becomes inactivated is determined randomly during early development, resulting in females being mosaic with respect to whether the maternal or paternal allele is inactivated. This mosaicism makes it technically challenging to separate the active and inactive chromosomes in bulk populations, and consequently it has been historically difficult to study X chromosome inactivation in human cells. Here we use long read sequencing of 31 single cell clones derived from primary human dermal fibroblasts from 7 donors aged 25-80 years, and generate a method to distinguish DNA methylation state of the active versus the inactive X chromosome. As expected, CpG islands (CGIs) on the inactive X chromosome have high levels of methylation, while CGIs on the active X chromosome are very lowly methylated. Notably, we observe substantial loss of DNA methylation across multiple CGIs on the inactive X chromosome in an age dependent manner. We also observe this DNA methylation erosion in bulk samples by quantifying CGI methylation levels across individual sequencing reads. The genes that show age-related erosion of CGI methylation are associated with increased total transcription suggesting this methylation erosion generates a transcriptional permissive state. Overall, our study provides evidence of erosion of X chromosome inactivation with age in cell lines derived from primary human samples and implicates a role for loss of DNA methylation in the increased dosage of X chromosome linked genes in females with age. These findings shed new light on the epigenetic instability of the inactive X chromosome during human ageing and may be linked to age-related cellular dysfunction in females.

items.title: Loss of SRF-driven contractility, not lymphatic smooth muscle cell loss, is the primary driver of age-associated collecting vessel decline
items.blurb: The lymphatic vasculature returns interstitial fluid to the blood circulation, a function that depends on rhythmic contraction of the smooth muscle cells (SMCs) surrounding collecting vessels. Lymph transport declines with age, a decline attributed largely to loss of SMCs from collecting vessels. We show that the principal change is not their loss but the loss of their contractile phenotype. In mouse ear collecting vessels, contractile protein expression declined with age and the vessels dilated, yet the majority of SMCs remained on the vessel wall. The decline extended to serum response factor (SRF), the transcription factor driving the smooth muscle contractile gene programme, and was mirrored by a loss of SRF-dependent contractile transcripts in published single-cell data from aged lymphatic muscle cells. Inducible deletion of Srf in mural cells reproduced this state, abolishing the contractile programme while leaving the cells in place and thereby excluding impaired SMC recruitment as the main mechanism. The resulting vessels became severely dilated and misshapen, whereas lymphatic capillaries were unaffected; endothelial identity, valve formation and lymphatic endothelial cell (LEC) number were all preserved, with enlargement instead reflecting increased LEC size. Intravital imaging showed loss of both rhythmic contraction and the contractile movement of individual SMCs, and Evans blue drainage to the inguinal lymph node was correspondingly reduced. Deletion of Srf after the contractile phenotype was established recapitulated this loss, showing that SRF is required continuously to maintain lymphatic SMC contractility and providing a genetic model of age-associated lymphatic dysfunction.

items.title: Endogenous activation of multiple stress-response pathways during meiosis promotes gamete fitness
items.blurb: Gametogenesis, the process of meiosis coupled to gamete formation, transforms diploid progenitor cells into haploid gametes through extensive cellular remodeling and rewiring of gene expression. Several stress-responsive transcription factors (TFs) are upregulated during gametogenesis, but whether the cellular mechanisms that handle environmental stress also support the success of this developmental process is largely unexplored. Here, we show that four stress-responsive TFs, Hsf1, Skn7, and the paralogs Msn2 and Msn4, are endogenously active during budding yeast gametogenesis in the absence of external stress and drive distinct gene expression programs. Simultaneous meiotic depletion of Msn2, Msn4, and Skn7 compromise the fitness of the resulting gametes. We identified just two TF-dependent targets, the antioxidant genes TSA1 and AHP1, as important for gamete fitness, directly connecting TF activity to the protection of meiotic progeny. Our results demonstrate that the activation of canonical stress-response regulators is built into the meiotic program and suggest that such pathways can be repurposed during development to safeguard cellular health.

items.title: Mutations in core Ccr4-NOT subunits manifest links to decapping rather than deadenylation in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
items.blurb: The mRNA polyadenosine tail (pA-tail) is gradually shortened in the cytoplasm by two main deadenylase complexes, Ccr4-NOT and Pan2/3, eventually leading to decapping and decay. The yeast Ccr4-NOT complex contains two deadenylases, Ccr4 and Pop2, and seven non-catalytic subunits. The functions of the latter are not yet fully understood. Here, we investigate the role of Ccr4-NOT in RNA metabolism in budding yeast. We show that steady-state mRNA pA-tail lengths increase with growth temperature, with this effect enhanced in ccr4{Delta} and pop2{Delta} cells, indicating a role for Ccr4-NOT in temperature-dependent mRNA regulation. Consistent with a functional divergence between species, we confirm that Ccr4 is the predominant deadenylase in yeast, whereas the Pop2 orthologs CNOT7/8 are the major deadenylases in human cells. Using Illumina and direct RNA sequencing, we characterize yeast strains defective in Ccr4-NOT, Pan2/3, or mRNA decapping. Unexpectedly, we show that loss of NOT1, NOT2, NOT4 or POP2 causes transcriptome and pA-tail changes resembling those of the decapping-factor mutants dhh1{Delta} and lsm1{Delta}, rather than of the principal deadenylase mutant ccr4{Delta}, and induces a mild stress response. Loss of Not2 or Not4 prolongs the half-lives of several mRNAs and causes growth defects comparable to decapping co-factor mutants. The mRNAs stabilized by loss of Not1-2-4 are distinct from those preferentially deadenylated by Ccr4-Pop2, suggesting different substrate targeting by Ccr4-NOT for non-overlapping functions in deadenylation and decapping.

items.title: Comparative landscape of extracellular vesicles across three pathogenic trematodes identifies a key conserved miRNA cargo involved in host liver fibrosis
items.blurb: Liver fibrosis caused by Schistosoma japonicum, Clonorchis sinensis, and Opisthorchis felineus represents a major global public health burden. Here, we systematically characterized extracellular vesicles (EVs) released by key stages of these parasites and uncovered, for the first time, a conserved repertoire of EV-derived miRNAs shared across all three species. By integrating animal models, single-cell RNA sequencing, and bioinformatic analyses, we comprehensively identified the targetome of miR-36-3p, a cross-species conserved miRNA cargo. Mechanistically, we found that miR-36-3p directly targets Atox1 in Kupffer cells, driving intracellular copper and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and thereby activating hepatic stellate cells. Strikingly, in vivo delivery of an AAV8-encoded miR-36-3p sponge markedly attenuated liver fibrosis across all three infection models. Collectively, these findings establish a conserved, parasite-derived EV miRNA cargo as a previously unrecognized driver of host liver pathology and identify it as a promising therapeutic target for preventing parasite-induced liver fibrosis.

items.title: A small molecule inhibits Neisseria gonorrhoeae pilus formation
items.blurb: Neisseria gonorrhoeae is becoming increasingly antimicrobial-resistant. N. gonorrhoeae requires the Type IV pilus (T4p) for pathogenesis, wherein the T4p promotes colonization through adherence to host cells and resistance to neutrophil killing. The pilus also is required for natural transformation and twitching motility. Collectively, these critical functions make the T4p an attractive drug target. Previously, we developed a high-throughput screen to identify compounds with activity against the zinc metalloprotease Mpg, which is involved in T4p biogenesis. Here, we identified a lead compound, SC144, that inhibits Mpg peptidoglycan-hydrolyzing activity in both N. gonorrhoeae and other bacteria encoding Mpg-like M23B metallopeptidase orthologs. Interestingly, SC144 targets Mpgs carboxypeptidase and endopeptidase activities. Importantly, SC144 inhibited N. gonorrhoeae colonization and prevented its survival in two primary human cell culture models of infection without toxic effects on these host cells. This work provides strong evidence that SC144 is a promising lead compound with anti-virulence activity against N. gonorrhoeae.

items.title: A Beta-to-Alpha seasonal coronavirus antibody signature identifies high and low responders to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination
items.blurb: Pre-existing immunity to endemic seasonal human coronaviruses may shape subsequent responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. We longitudinally profiled 775 healthcare workers using a systems immunology machine learning framework and found that a recursive feature elimination cross-validation model classified individuals in the top and bottom quartiles of SARS-CoV-2 Spike IgG responses (AUC=0.72, empirical P<0.001). This predictive signature was prominently driven by a baseline bias toward Beta-coronavirus relative to Alpha-coronavirus Spike reactivity.

items.title: NOTCH3 p.R544C Drives Early Neurovascular Unit Dysfunction through Blood-Brain Barrier Failure, Complement Signalling and Metabolic Dysregulation
items.blurb: Cerebral small vessel disease is a major cause of stroke and vascular cognitive impairment, yet the mechanisms that initiate neurovascular dysfunction before irreversible brain injury remain poorly defined. CADASIL, caused by cysteine-altering NOTCH3 mutations, provides a genetically tractable model to resolve these early events. Here, we investigated the Asian-enriched NOTCH3 p.R544C variant and tested whether early disease emerges through interconnected blood-brain barrier (BBB), inflammatory, and metabolic dysfunction. NOTCH3 p.R544C iPSC-derived endothelial cells showed impaired angiogenesis and migration, reduced barrier resistance, disrupted tight-junction organisation, and altered vascular, adhesion, and extracellular-matrix programmes. In multicellular BBB-like microtissues, these defects propagated across the neurovascular unit, producing disorganised vascular networks, enlarged luminal structures, and increased permeability, establishing BBB failure as an early disease layer. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed coordinated loss of endothelial BBB transport and efflux programmes with astrocytic complement, innate immune, and matrix-remodelling activation. Secretome profiling and patient-plasma measurements converged on complement- and matrix-associated mediators, including C1S and CLU, identifying complement-matrix activation as a second interconnected layer. Importantly, combined cilostazol and isosorbide mononitrate treatment improved barrier function and reduced selected complement- and matrix-associated proteins in mutant microtissues, supporting pharmacological reversibility of components of this early disease programme. Seahorse analysis further demonstrated reduced mitochondrial respiratory capacity associated with NOTCH3 p.R544C. In vivo, three-month-old mutant mice showed altered cerebral pyruvate metabolism and early microvascular abnormalities, whereas six-month-old mice developed more prominent extracellular-matrix, inflammatory, and gliovascular changes, supporting an age-dependent transition from early metabolic dysregulation to broader neurovascular remodelling. Together, these findings define NOTCH3 p.R544C CADASIL as an early multicellular neurovascular disorder organised across three interconnected mechanistic layers: BBB failure, complement-matrix signalling, and metabolic dysregulation, while identifying early BBB-centred dysfunction as a potentially tractable state before advanced cerebrovascular injury develops.

items.title: Myeloid DNA methyltransferase 3A loss impairs macrophage polarization and promotes inflammation, phagocytosis and hepatosplenomegaly
items.blurb: Background: Genetic variants in the de novo DNA methyltransferase DNMT3A increase inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) risk, yet the mechanisms linking defective DNMT3A to IBD remain unclear. As macrophages gatekeep immune homeostasis, we characterized how myeloid-specific DNMT3A loss affects monocytic differentiation and inflammatory properties. Methods: We generated myeloid-specific Dnmt3a-deficient mice (Dnmt3a-LysM) via LysM-cre. Deletion was confirmed in gut lamina propria CD11b+ cells and bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM). M1/M2-polarized BMDMs were characterized by methylation profiling, mRNA-sequencing, flow cytometry, arginase/NOS activity, phagocytosis (FITC-zymosan), and co-culture with wounded ModeK epithelial monolayers. Colitis was induced using dextran sodium sulfate (DSS). Results: Dnmt3a expression was induced by M2 and repressed by inflammatory stimuli in wild-type (Dnmt3afl/fl) BMDMs. Upon IL-4/IL-13 stimulation, Dnmt3a-LysM BMDMs exhibited heightened ERK1/2 and PI3K signaling, reduced M2 markers, increased pro-inflammatory Irg1/Tnf transcripts, and acquired M1-like features; amplified in BMDMs from aged (>34 weeks) mice (disrupted morphology, enhanced phagocytosis, reduced arginase and elevated iNOS activity). These cells impaired epithelial regeneration in co-culture. In vivo, young Dnmt3a-LysM mice showed splenic immune alterations and DSS-colitis hypersensitivity. Aged Dnmt3a-LysM mice displayed altered bone marrow architecture, hepatosplenomegaly, and myeloproliferation. Conclusions: Dnmt3a is required for physiological macrophage polarization. Its myeloid-specific loss drives pro-inflammatory skewing, potentially contributing to IBD pathogenesis.

items.title: Cross-Species Dynamics of Transposable Elements in Aging Female Visceral Adipose Tissues
items.blurb: Transposable elements (TEs) make up nearly half of mammalian genomes and are increasingly implicated in genomic instability, cellular stress responses, aging, and age-related disease. Recent past research has highlighted their significant involvement in disease models such as cancer and Alzheimer's disease (AD), though much remains to be unraveled regarding these genomic insertions. In this study, we explore the involvement of TEs in aging female mouse and human visceral adipose tissue (VAT) using 10x single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) data analyzed with the computational tool SoloTE. By assessing the TE-annotated snRNA-seq count matrix using Seurat, we found that retrotransposons-specifically short interspersed nuclear elements (SINEs) and long interspersed nuclear elements (LINEs) on chromosomes 1 and 19-are significantly upregulated in aging female human VAT and in potential senescent cells (CDKN1A^+). Although changes in mouse VAT were less pronounced, long terminal repeats (LTRs) were predominant in aging mouse cells. Furthermore, analysis of upregulated features in aging and CDKN1A^+ female human VAT cells revealed that LINE and SINE TEs embedded within specific gene loci-most notably CUX1, SOD2, C3, NAMPT, ALDH1A3, IL6, and the non-coding RNA LOC105375913-exhibit a positive regulatory relationship with their host genes. Specifically, higher TE expression may directly upregulate host gene expression (e.g., C3 TEs driving C3 upregulation). Consistently ranking at the top of differentially expressed feature lists, these TEs act as potential drivers of aging and cellular senescence in female human VAT and can be plausible targets without risk of disruption of multiple biological systems.

items.title: Hyphal differentiation and cell wall remodeling in Trametes versicolor underlie a layered architecture in pure mycelium materials
items.blurb: Background: Pure mycelium materials grown at the air-liquid interface are promising leather alternatives, yet they are generally treated as homogeneous sheets of fungal biomass. Because basidiomycetes differentiate their hyphae into generative, skeletal and ligative cell types, the properties of such materials may instead arise from an internal tissue organisation. In this study, cell types produced by the trimitic white-rot fungus Trametes versicolor during Liquid State Surface Fermentation were characterized and the impact of their spatial organisation, mechanics and cell wall composition on the resulting material was analysed. Results: Optic and electron microscopy revealed the mats are not homogeneous but consist of two layers: a dense bottom layer of thin-walled generative hyphae in contact with the liquid medium, and a looser, air-exposed top layer made of thick-walled skeletal hyphae. Both layers had comparable hyphal diameters (2.43 {+/-} 0.42 and 2.33 {+/-} 0.50 {micro}m), but the skeletal hyphae in the mat were roughly half the diameter of their fruiting-body counterparts (5.10 {+/-} 1.05 {micro}m). Untreated mats stress-strain curves displayed sequential failure: brittle fracture of the generative bottom layer followed by ductile failure of the skeletal layer. The two faces also differed in wettability, the top being hydrophobic and highly adhesive and the bottom hydrophilic. Solid-state NMR showed extensive rigid cell wall remodelling between the two cell types: alpha-1,3-glucan accounted for about one third of the rigid polysaccharides in the generative layer but was undetectable in the skeletal layer, which contained approximately 74% beta-1,3-glucan and 26% chitin and was overall more rigid and more lipid-rich. Conclusions: These results show that Trametes versicolor differentiates into a very specific type of skeletal hyphae in liquid state surface fermentation, which involves remodelling of the molecular architecture of the cell wall rather than a simple thickening of it, and that the mechanical and surface behaviour of the material can be traced to that remodelling and to the cellular organisation.

items.title: Optimizing environmental conditions for PALM imaging of the nuclear pore complex labeled with the photoconvertible fluorescent protein mEos4b.
items.blurb: Green-to-red photoconvertible fluorescent proteins (PCFPs) are smart fluorophores used in several nanoscopy approaches based on single-molecule localization microscopy (SMLM). To optimize the achievable spatial resolution and facilitate molecular counting in these approaches, PCFPs should deliver a high effective labeling efficiency (ELE). Here, to evaluate the ELE provided by mEos4b, a performant PCFP, we designed a constitutive Nup96-mEos4b protein fusion in the nuclear pore complex (NPC) of U2OS cells, and performed PhotoActivated Localization Microscopy (PALM) imaging of NPCs in fixed cells under different environmental conditions. We find that removal of oxygen improves the ELE by more than 20%. Overall, using HEPES as buffer in deuterated and deoxygenated water delivers the highest quality PALM images of NPCs labeled with mEos4b. These conditions should be beneficial for quantitative PALM or Minimal Fluorescence Photon Fluxes Microscopy (Minflux) experiments in fixed cells. We propose a photophysical scheme that accounts for the observed improvements in the absence of oxygen.

items.title: BEguided: Systematic guide and base editor evaluation for precision single-nucleotide editing
items.blurb: Base editing enables precise nucleotide substitutions without introducing DNA double-strand breaks, but identifying optimal editor-guide combinations remains challenging because PAM compatibility, editing-window positioning, bystander modifications, and off-target effects must be considered simultaneously. Here, we introduce BEguided, an integrated computational platform for variant-specific guide RNA design and systematic comparison across 38 predefined base-editor profiles, with support for user-defined editors. BEguided incorporates single-nucleotide variants directly into target sequences, eliminating the need for customized reference genomes, while its companion tool, BEguidedOFF, provides base-editing-aware off-target prediction. To demonstrate the utility of this approach, we systematically assessed the accessibility of the 1,000 most frequent ABE-editable cancer mutations to adenine base editing. Under stringent guide-quality, bystander-editing, and predicted off-target criteria, only 7 mutations could be targeted using SpCas9-ABE8e. Expanding the analysis to additional SpCas9-compatible adenine base editors increased this number to 30, while inclusion of SaCas9, relaxed-PAM Cas9-NG/SpG variants, and PAM-less SpRY further expanded the number of potentially targetable mutations to 100, 156, and 238, respectively. These findings highlight the substantial impact of editor selection on mutation accessibility and establish BEguided as a versatile framework for identifying and prioritizing base-editing strategies for disease-associated variants. BEguided is available at https://beguided.buchholzlab.org.

items.title: Identification of seven candidate structured noncoding RNA motifs in protists by comparative genomics
items.blurb: Protists represent a highly diverse assemblage of predominantly unicellular eukaryotes, including protozoa, algae, and slime molds. Their essential roles in global ecosystems, along with their significance as human parasites, underscore the need for a deeper understanding of their conserved genetic elements. In this study, we employed an integrated computational approach combining CMfinder and R-scape to systematically identify and evaluate structured non-coding RNA (ncRNA) motifs across protist genomes. Through rigorous assessment and functional annotation, we report seven conserved structured ncRNAs that are likely functional RNA motifs involved in regulating the synthesis of the carbon fixation protein ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (RuBisCO), the light-harvesting and transfer protein phycocyanin, subunits of photosystems I and II, as well as mRNA splicing regulation. Notably, we also identified a structured ncRNA motif that may possess a dual function, capable of bidirectionally regulating the photosystem genes psaI and psbJ simultaneously. Our findings provide valuable insights into the diversity and functional significance of structured ncRNAs in microbial eukaryotes.

items.title: ADP-ribosylation governs the repair of topoisomerase IIIβ-induced nucleic acid damage
items.blurb: Abortive DNA and RNA-linked covalent cleavage complexes formed by the unique dual-activity human topoisomerase III{beta} (TOP3B) disrupt nucleic acid metabolism and can promote cancer cell death. Here, we identify poly(ADP-ribosylation) (PARylation) as a key pathway that regulates the repair and stability of both DNA- and RNA-linked TOP3B cleavage complexes (TOP3Bccs). We show that accumulated TOP3Bccs undergo rapid PARylation in a PARP1-dependent manner and that this modification is dynamically reversed by poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG). Mass spectrometry identified major ADP-ribosylation sites on TOP3B, and disruption of these sites impaired TOP3Bcc homeostasis. Mechanistically, PARylation recruits flap endonuclease 1 (FEN1) to excise and repair TOP3Bccs. Persistent PARylation caused by PARG inhibition recruits the deubiquitylating enzyme (DUB) USP10 to promote TOP3Bcc deubiquitylation and thereby stabilize TOP3Bccs, presumably by preventing proteasomal degradation. Together, this study identifies a dynamic PARylation-mediated pathway that coordinates the repair of abortive TOP3Bccs. This pathway defines a critical mechanism of TOP3Bcc homeostasis and may influence cancer cell responses to TOP3B-targeting agents.

items.title: TrES-seq integrates single-cell RNA and nanobody-based histone mark profiles to decode epigenetic and transcriptional axes of cell identity
items.blurb: Histone post-translational modifications and gene expression jointly shape cellular identity and activity. However, systematically assessing their heterogeneity and functional interdependence requires high-quality multimodal single-cell readouts, whose generation still faces significant technological challenges. Here, we developed TrES-seq (transcriptional and epigenetic state sequencing), a method that integrates scRNA-seq with species-specific nanobody Tn5 fusion proteins to jointly profile RNA and two histone modifications in the same cells and across multiple samples. In human tonsils, single-cell H3K27ac, H3K27me3, H3K9me3, and RNA data in >25,000 cells revealed a one-to-many relationship where heterogeneous transcriptional states shared similar epigenetic profiles. For example, naive and memory B cells were transcriptionally different but epigenetically indistinguishable, while the epigenetic status of enhancers but not promoters separated germinal center from naive and memory B cells. Moreover, naturally occurring and treatment-induced cell state transitions revealed broad transcriptional changes occurring among genes that already exhibited and retained an epigenetically active state. Overall, TrES-seq provides a robust and cost-effective platform to determine how epigenetic states influence transcriptional heterogeneity, shaping cell phenotypes and function in different physiological and pathological contexts.

items.title: Emergence of mobile fosA3-blaCTX-M-65 with mcr-1.1 and tet(X4) on conjugative plasmids in avian pathogenic Escherichia coli from industrial poultry in Pakistan
items.blurb: The emergence of plasmid-mediated resistance to critically important antimicrobials poses a growing threat to global health. Here we report the first genomic evidence of plasmid-mediated fosA3 and blaCTX-M-65 coexisting with mcr-1.1 and tet(X4) in multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli from clinically healthy broiler chickens in Pakistan. Among 1,677 high-quality genomes collected through antimicrobial resistance surveillance in Punjab, Pakistan, three isolates recovered between 2022 and 2024 harboured all four resistance determinants. Hybrid genome assemblies showed that fosA3 and blaCTX-M-65 were co-located on IncHI2A plasmids, whereas mcr-1.1 and tet(X4) were carried on separate IncI2 and IncFIA/IncFIC plasmids, all predicted to be conjugative; in one isolate the tet(X4) contig did not circularise. The isolates belonged to sequence type 93 and exhibited resistance to fosfomycin, colistin, tigecycline and cefotaxime. Comparative genomic analysis revealed highly conserved IncHI2A plasmid backbones, with an additional integron-associated resistance region in the 2024 isolates, suggesting acquisition of accessory resistance determinants. Resistance to three last-line antimicrobial classes and a canonical virulence profile now coexist on conjugative plasmids in poultry E. coli, a combination that favours co-selection and argues for plasmid-resolved surveillance in poultry production.

items.title: Electron Transport Chain-inhibiting fungicides increase resistance to widely used azole antifungals
items.blurb: Rising antifungal resistance in human and crop fungal pathogens poses significant challenges. Azole-based antifungals that inhibit ergosterol biosynthesis are a key first-line treatment for human fungal infections. Importantly, azole-based ergosterol-inhibiting fungicides are also widely used in agriculture alongside electron transport chain (ETC) Complex III inhibiting compounds. However, it is unknown whether the combined use of these distinct fungicides is entirely synergistic. We find that exposure of fission yeast, Schizosaccharomyces pombe to ETC-Complex III inhibitors, prior to or simultaneously with azoles, attenuates azole efficacy by inducing mitochondrial dysfunction. Our analyses show that reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation as a result of ETC inhibition activates oxidative stress response pathways thereby decreasing azole potency. Related responses in pathogenic fungi indicate that the use of ETC inhibiting fungicides in agriculture may inadvertently promote azole resistance. We conclude that the use of specific fungicide combinations should be re-evaluated in order to preserve both their clinical and agricultural effectiveness.

items.title: Multi-Cohort Blood Transcriptomic Meta-Analysis of Active Pulmonary Tuberculosis: Reproducibility of a 50-Gene Interferon Signature and Benchmarking of a 4-Gene Classifier
items.blurb: Background: Most blood transcriptomic signatures for tuberculosis (TB) come from a single population or a single platform. Few have been built by meta-analysis and benchmarked against published signatures. Methods: We meta-analysed three UK blood transcriptomic datasets (two Illumina microarray, one RNA-seq; 247 samples: 87 active pulmonary TB (PTB), 160 healthy controls (HC)). GSE107991 reanalyses the Berry test set, and two discovery datasets overlap Sweeney's discovery data, so the datasets are not fully independent. Genes were retained if they replicated in all three studies (FDR 1.5, FDR < 0.01). Performance was estimated in GSE28623 (The Gambia, n = 83) and GSE56153 (Indonesia, n = 36); direction was checked in GSE34608 (Germany, n = 26) and GSE81746 (India, n = 6). A LASSO and random-forest classifier was compared with the Berry 393-gene and Sweeney 3-gene signatures. Immune composition was assessed with MCPcounter and CIBERSORTx. Results: We identified a 50-gene core signature dominated by interferon-stimulated genes. All 50 were upregulated and reached FDR < 0.05 in every dataset. ssGSEA gave an AUC of 0.830 (95% CI 0.743-0.917) in GSE28623 and 0.941 (0.868-1.000) in GSE56153. Direction agreement was 95.7% in Germany and 95.8% in India. PTB versus latent TB infection gave 0.848 (0.756-0.940). LASSO selected four genes (BATF2, ANKRD22, GBP5 and EPSTI1). The frozen classifier gave an external AUC of 0.864 (0.785-0.944). The Sweeney 3-gene score, re-tested in one of its validation cohorts, reached 0.912 and exceeded the 50-gene score (47/50 genes; Holm p = 0.0234). Berry 393-gene scoring gave 0.910 with directions reconstructed from GSE19439 (Holm p = 0.0071 versus the 50-gene score). The signed score is a reconstruction, not Berry's published score. MCPcounter showed myeloid expansion and lymphoid suppression; CIBERSORTx recovered the former but not the broader lymphoid suppression. Conclusions: The 50-gene signature was consistent across three overlapping UK discovery datasets. External evaluation was partial, comprising AUCs for 47 of the 50 genes in two cohorts and direction concordance in two smaller cohorts. This is a benchmarking study, not a claim of superiority: the Sweeney 3-gene and signed Berry scores were higher, and the 4-gene classifier did not differ significantly from Sweeney. The classifier warrants prospective validation. The Berry and Sweeney comparisons are not independent.

items.title: Environmental heterogeneity and microbial community architecture shape N2O fluxes in intertidal coastal sediments
items.blurb: Seagrass meadows are key ''blue carbon ecosystems'', yet their contribution to nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions remains poorly constrained. We investigated environmental and microbial descriptors of N2O fluxes in intertidal sediments of Arcachon Bay, home to Europe's largest Zostera noltii meadow. At six sites, we measured in situ N2O fluxes in adjacent bare and vegetated sediments and characterized sediment properties, N2O-cycling genes using qPCR and targeted metagenomics, and microbial co-occurrence networks. Fluxes ranged from -3.7 to 8.4 mol N2O m-2 d-1. Spatial location was the strongest descriptor of flux variation, with inner-bay sites showing higher emissions associated with environmental conditions, carbon accumulation, pH, and microbial community characteristics. Vegetation effects were comparatively small and site-dependent. Metagenomic descriptors of N2O-cycling genes were more informative than qPCR-based descriptors. Taxa associated with nirS (Thiohalophilus), nirK (Planktotalea) and nosZ1 (Roseobacter) were identified as potential contributors to N2O production or reduction, respectively. These findings indicate that spatially structured environmental conditions and microbial community characteristics better describe N2O flux variation than seagrass presence alone. Measurements across tidal and seasonal cycles are needed to establish the temporal consistency of these patterns.

items.title: Genomic Characterization of a Typical Enteropathogenic Escherichia coli Isolate from an Egyptian Fruit Bat, Rousettus aegyptiacus from Coastal Kenya
items.blurb: Enteropathogenic Escherichia coli (EPEC) are responsible for significant morbidity and mortality cases among young children under the age of five, particularly in low- and middle-income countries.
